1.explanation:
1. src/config/format.ts – defines the shape of the format-specific options in the config schema; if html.crossref isn’t declared or defaulted here, the downstream code never sees it.  
2. src/command/render/filters.ts – this file picks which Lua filters to invoke based on top-level metadata.crossref; it doesn’t inspect metadata.format.html.crossref, so format-scoped disabling is ignored.  
3. src/command/render/crossref.ts – contains the logic that reads metadata.crossref settings and marshals them into arguments for the crossref filter; it only considers global metadata.crossref, not format.html.crossref.  
4. src/command/render/pandoc.ts – is responsible for merging document metadata (including nested metadata.format.*) and passing it to Pandoc; it must be updated so that format-scoped crossref flags override or augment the top-level crossref settings when building the Pandoc call.  
5. resources/filters/crossref/options.lua – the Lua filter uses the metadata it is given to decide whether to number and link references; it expects a boolean crossref flag in meta.crossref.*. Because the TS code never passes html.crossref:false into meta.crossref, the filter never disables numbering.  

Together, these files control how "crossref: false" under a particular output format is surfaced in the Pandoc filter pipeline. Fixing them will allow format.html.crossref:false to actually suppress cross-referencing in that format.
1.bug_scenario:
When a user sets “crossref: false” under the html format in the document YAML (for example in tests/docs/crossrefs/false.qmd), the HTML output should have all figure and table cross-references disabled (no “Fig. 1”, no “Table 1”, etc.). The test (tests/integration/formats/html/crossref-false.test.ts) verifies that no “Fig. 1” string appears in the generated HTML. However, today the numbering still appears, so format-specific “crossref: false” is silently ignored.

The attached screenshot shows a YAML front matter with:

  format:
    html:
      crossref: false

…and yet the rendered output still contains “Fig. 1”.

2.explanation:
1. resources/filters/crossref/options.lua  
   • This file reads the document’s metadata to determine whether cross-references should be numbered, and what prefixes to use. It currently only looks under top-level `meta.crossref` rather than at `meta.format.html.crossref`, so it never sees `crossref: false` when it’s set in the format block.

2. resources/filters/crossref/qmd.lua  
   • This helper script merges Quarto-specific front-matter into the filter’s options. It needs to be updated to propagate `format.html.crossref` down into the filter’s own config.

3. resources/filters/crossref/index.lua  
   • This is the entry point for the Lua crossref filter. It imports the options module and applies the numbering logic. Because options.lua never sees the format-specific override, index.lua always numbers figures in HTML.

4. src/command/render/filters.ts  
   • This TypeScript file builds the list of Pandoc filters (including the crossref filter) and passes along document metadata. It is responsible for serializing the metadata JSON that the Lua filters read. It must be updated so that when invoking Pandoc for HTML, it flattens the `format.html.crossref` value into the top-level metadata that the filter expects.

By updating these four files to look for and honor `meta.format.<format>.crossref: false`, the Lua crossref filter will correctly disable numbering in HTML when requested.
2.bug_scenario: The user wants to be able to disable all cross-reference numbering for HTML output by setting `format: html: crossref: false` in their Quarto document’s YAML header. However, even when `crossref: false` is set under `format.html`, figure references like “Fig. 1” still appear in the generated HTML. The screenshots show a red underline under `crossref: false` and the HTML output still containing “Fig. 1”. This indicates that the HTML crossref filters are not picking up the `crossref: false` setting when it is nested under `format.html`.
